name: maestro
purpose: Drive the mobile app on a device.

entryPoints.name: app
entryPoints.purpose: The app ID of the app under test, for example com.example.shop.

entryPoints.name: device
entryPoints.purpose: The ID of the simulator or emulator that runs the app.

delegatedInstruction: Use the app and device of the instance. Prefix every Maestro call with XDG_STATE_HOME="{workFolder}/maestro-state" to move default test logs into the work folder. Give --device <device> before the command. Write flows in {workFolder} with appId: <app> and --- as the header. Start with a flow that has - launchApp for the app of the instance, then read the screen. A Home screen or another app on the screen means that the app is not started yet, not an error of the test. Put steps that need no screen read in between in one flow. Run maestro --device <device> test <flow> --test-output-dir="{workFolder}/maestro" --debug-output="{workFolder}/maestro". Read with maestro --device <device> hierarchy --compact only for a decision or a check. Use text or an id from the latest hierarchy for each screen. Never invent a selector. On iOS, tap a switch with point: inside the bounds of the element with checked or value. A tap on its row label or id can leave it unchanged. If an action target is off screen, scroll. If it is missing, wait one second. Read the hierarchy again and retry once. If the action still fails, close the test as error with the hierarchy excerpt. After an action, if a value still looks unchanged, read the hierarchy once more before you record it. Keep assertions out of the flow. For relaunch, stop and launch the app. If it opens at its root screen, navigate again. Attach a short hierarchy excerpt with --evidence -:view_hierarchy when it shows the result. When appearance is the evidence, use takeScreenshot and attach the PNG with --evidence <path>:screenshot. Do not run start-device, studio, clearState, or a new install of the app.
